transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SA), Martin (ZenithCloud), Priya (ZenithCloud), Luca (ZenithCloud security)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Redwood Private offering on ZenithCloud Marketplace, and joint solution integration points (networking, auth, billing). Agreed to run compatibility benchmarks on Zenith staging, draft reference arch diagram, and exchange SOC2 + marketplace artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood. We have Daniel and Sofia from the tech side. 
[00:15] Martin: Hi, Martin here from ZenithCloud partnerships, thanks Aisha. Priya and Luca from our platform and security teams are on as well.
[00:30] Daniel: cool, we'll jump into architecture stuff, but first can you outline the marketplace mode you're thinking — listing as a managed private offering vs a marketplace AMI style?
[00:45] Priya: Our goal is to offer Redwood as a first-class listing in our marketplace with an option for customers to deploy into their VPC via a private control plane. Ideally we want a SaaS-managed control plane but with VPC peering for data egress rules.
[01:10] Sofia: got it. Redwood has a Private deployment model that supports VPC peering or private link. We typically ship a customer-managed runtime or a managed runtime with private connectivity. There's a couple of auth and KMS considerations.
[01:30] Luca: speaking of KMS, we need to understand how keys are managed; is customer-managed KMS supported? Also audit logs and retention — SOC2 stuff.
[01:45] Aisha: yes, we support customer KMS/HSM integrations for Private. We'll share our SOC2 package and typical audit log schema. (brief pause) sorry that last part came out a bit clipped on my end.
[02:00] Martin: no worries, transcription is fine. For the marketplace listing, we have a checklist — tile, support SLA, billing integration. How does Redwood typically handle billing for Dedicated/Private through partners?
[02:20] Daniel: two common flows: marketplace metered billing where Zenith invoices and we reconcile, or direct billing with a referral. For Dedicated it's usually via a commit contract. We'll align with your commercial team.
[02:35] Priya: from a technical point we need an integration spec for service deployment — container images, helm charts, or an AMI?
[02:50] Sofia: we prefer using our reference architectures: we can provide terraform modules and a helm chart for the runtime. For marketplace quickstart, an infrastructure-as-code reference is best. We'll share a reference arch diagram.
[03:05] Martin: perfect. On networking — do you require VPC peering only, or do you support private link / transit gateway patterns? Some of our customers are strict about peering limitations.
[03:25] Daniel: Redwood supports both peering and private link; for high-volume low-latency customers we recommend peering + dedicated capacity. For broad marketplace we set private link as fallback because it's simpler for restricted networks.
[03:45] Priya: any port / CIDR requirements? We have to validate with our infra teams.
[03:55] Sofia: typical egress ports 443 and a few management ports; we'll provide a minimal CIDR set. We also have options to run the inference runtime entirely inside the customer's VPC if they want on-prem style isolation.
[04:15] Luca: regarding IAM and SSO — SAML is mandatory for us. Does Redwood support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:30] Daniel: yes SAML for auth and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC is supported at org and route level. We'll share our SSO integration guide.
[04:45] Aisha: also, for marketplace listings we need a short security questionnaire and some legal artifacts. We'll send a pack.
[05:00] Martin: great. On the reference architecture, do you have a recommended pattern for KV cache persistence and across-region fallback? Some customers need multi-region low-latency.
[05:20] Sofia: we use an in-memory KV cache for active sessions and optional cross-region replication for model state. For multi-region we recommend regional inference endpoints with smart routing. That avoids cross-region latency for token loops.
[05:40] Priya: OK that sounds like the diagram we need. Can you mark which parts run in Zenith-managed infra vs Redwood-managed control plane?
[05:55] Sofia: yes — we'll annotate: control plane (Redwood managed) vs data plane (customer/VPC or Zenith-managed runtime). For marketplace we can provide either option but need to flag network egress and data residency.
[06:15] Martin: data residency is big for some of our enterprise customers — they require logs never leave region. Can Redwood enforce local-only logging?
[06:30] Daniel: yes, we can configure region-bound logging and retention policies; we'll outline defaults and per-customer overrides.
[06:45] Luca: on encryption at rest, we need certs that integrate with our KMS. If Redwood manages anything, are the keys customer-owned?
[06:58] Sofia: we support customer-owned KMS for encryption at rest and envelope encryption. When Redwood manages the runtime we still can accept customer KMS policies for critical secrets.
[07:15] Martin: very helpful. Switching to marketplace metadata — we need a short tech blurb, screenshots, and tiers. Does Redwood have a recommended tile for demo vs production?
[07:35] Aisha: yes, we have marketplace asset templates: one for trial (hosted) and one for production (dedicated/private). We'll send the templates and example screenshots.
[07:50] Priya: for trial flows, what are quotas and quotas enforcement? Some customers start with small token caps and grow.
[08:05] Daniel: we support quotas by API key / org and rate limiting; we can default to soft caps for trials and then switch to committed throughput for production.
[08:20] Martin: does the marketplace support offering a managed demo environment that spins up per-customer?
[08:30] Sofia: yes, but it's more common to provide a demo account (hosted) or quickstart that deploys into a sandbox VPC. For fully managed per-customer demos it's doable but has operational overhead.
[08:45] Martin: understood.
[09:00] Priya: you mentioned benchmarks earlier — what's the recommended benchmark suite? Latency, tokens/sec, model variants?
[09:15] Daniel: we typically run throughput (tokens/sec) at 128 and 512 context lengths, tail latency p95/p99, and memory/VRAM telemetry. For marketplace compatibility we'll do a light run on a single node image to validate model startup and kernel support.
[09:40] Martina (note: transcription sometimes swaps names): sorry, my mic cut — martin here. Can we also validate quantized model support? some customers require 4-bit deployments.
[09:55] Sofia: yes, quantization support varies by model; Redwood has quantization profiles and we can recommend model variants for lowest-cost inference. We'll include recommended quantization and profiles in the reference arch doc.
[10:15] Luca: from security perspective, can we get a sample network flow diagram and a list of logs/endpoints we capture for audit?
[10:30] Daniel: yes, we'll provide a sample network flow diagram, list of API endpoints, and the audit log schema (timestamp, actor, action, resource).
[10:45] Martin: great. Moving on to joint solution go-to-market — we want to co-author a reference architecture doc and possibly run a webinar. Are you open to co-marketing?
[11:00] Aisha: absolutely, we typically do a joint webinar and a reference architecture blog post. We'll propose timelines after the tech validation.
[11:15] Priya: timeline — some customers are looking to pilot in Q3; what's realistic from Redwood side?
[11:30] Aisha: if benchmarks are green and the reference arch is approved, a pilot could start in 6-8 weeks. So Q3 pilots are doable.
[11:45] Daniel: operationally we'll need access to a Zenith staging account and a small test dataset. Also a point-of-contact for infra provisioning.
[12:00] Priya: that's us — I'll be the POC and will share staging creds after we set an NDA/secure transfer.
[12:15] Martin: on legal — marketplace listing requires a data processing addendum for EU customers. Do you have a DPA template?
[12:30] Aisha: yes, we have a standard DPA and can adjust for regional requirements; we'll attach to the packet.
[12:45] Luca: one more security nit — do you support log redaction for PII in traces? Some customers want PII stripped before logs leave their VPC.
[13:00] Sofia: we can configure redaction rules and local-only telemetry. We'll detail which fields are redacted by default and which need an explicit opt-in.
[13:15] Priya: excellent. For the marketplace listing process, what's the gating review? Does Zenith require a security review before listing?
[13:30] Martin: yes, we run a security review; SOC2 plus a short tech checklist, then we do functional verification in staging. After that the tile goes live.
[13:45] Aisha: sounds straightforward. We'll pack the SOC2, SSO guide, reference arch, and marketplace assets into one packet.
[14:00] Daniel: quick note on model variants — customers sometimes want Redwood to host multiple model families. For the marketplace, do you want a single default model set or an option to pick?
[14:20] Martin: marketplace customers like an easy default plus advanced options. We can surface model variants as plan tiers.
[14:35] Sofia: okay we'll include recommended defaults and cost-estimates per model/quantization. That will help your tile pricing.
[14:50] Priya: about monitoring — what telemetry do you surface to customers? We need to show resource usage and latency metrics in the Zenith console.
[15:05] Daniel: we can emit metrics to Prometheus endpoints, push to CloudWatch, or send via a webhook. For marketplace integration, an exporter to your metrics backend is usually easiest.
[15:20] Martin: that would be ideal, we can accept CloudWatch or a Prometheus scrape target.
[15:35] Aisha: ok note to share exporter config.
[15:45] (longer discussion on benchmarking details and test plan, some cross talk)
[22:30] Daniel: returning to the compatibility run — we need to verify kernel support for the models you expect to surface. Priya, can you share the top three models customers will request?
[22:45] Priya: mostly open models: small Llama-family ops, some MPT variants, and one bespoke LLM from a partner; we'll list exact names.
[23:00] Sofia: good, we'll map quantization profile and kernel compatibility per model. Expect a short report within a week of the run.
[23:20] Martin: on support SLAs for marketplace customers, do you provide 24/7?
[23:35] Aisha: for marketplace listings we can offer standard business hours support and an optional premium SLA for production customers. We'll include tiered support options.
[23:50] Luca: any specific compliance for EU customers we should call out? Data residency, KMS, and DPA are primary.
[24:05] Daniel: yes those are the main ones. Also note that Private deployments can be provisioned in EU regions only to satisfy residency.
[24:20] Priya: can Redwood run in our GovCloud-like regions? We have closed regions for regulated customers.
[24:35] Sofia: we have an on-prem/private package that can be installed in air-gapped environments; I'll share the install docs and hardware guidance.
[24:50] Martin: excellent.
[25:00] (brief pause, some background noise)
[25:30] Aisha: let's recap next steps — action items we'll put in the meeting notes but to summarize: Redwood to share reference arch + SOC2 + SSO guide + marketplace assets, Redwood to run compatibility benchmark on Zenith staging, Zenith to share staging access and model list, and both to align on timeline for a Q3 pilot.
[25:55] Priya: yes I'll share staging network details and a POC contact; expect that by Monday.
[26:10] Daniel: small tech question — for KV cache warmup, do you pre-load common prompts or rely on live traffic? We've had customers ask about warm start.
[26:30] Sofia: we support prefix cache pre-loading for predictable workloads; we'll include guidance on seeding caches and eviction policies.
[26:50] Martin: will that impact billing? if you pre-load caches for demo tenants, does Redwood bill token usage?
[27:05] Aisha: good question — for demo and pilot we can set a billing exemption; for production it's counted. We'll document the pilot credit policy.
[27:20] Priya: on the marketplace tile, can we show an embedded demo (iframe) or do you prefer links out?
[27:35] Aisha: most marketplaces prefer links out for live demos, but a sandbox iframe is possible if it's lightweight. We'll advise on best practices.
[27:50] Luca: last security Q from me — are there standard penetration test reports you can share?
[28:05] Daniel: yes, we have a recent pentest summary and remediation notes; we'll include redacted reports and an executive summary.
[28:20] Martin: great. Anything else?
[28:30] (crosstalk)
[28:45] Priya: timeline reminder — we need the marketplace artifacts to begin review next week to stay on schedule.
[28:55] Aisha: we'll prioritize the assets and aim to send the packet by Friday EOD.
[29:10] Daniel: technical note — for the benchmark run, we'll need a small instance type and sample load generator; we'll provide scripts.
[29:25] Priya: we'll provision a t3-like instance? maybe a c6i? we'll coordinate sizing offline.
[29:45] Sofia: ok we'll provide recommended instance types per model family.
[30:00] Martin: can you also provide a small whitelist of IPs for staging so our security team can permit inbound?
[30:15] Aisha: yes, we'll include IP ranges and ports in the packet.
[30:30] (some side conversation about marketing assets and joint webinar scheduling)
[31:20] Aisha: we'll propose a date range for the webinar after pilot conclusions; initial PR joint blog could align with listing launch.
[31:35] Priya: that works.
[31:50] Luca: Security will do a more thorough review once we have the audit logs and architecture doc.
[32:05] Daniel: note to include retention defaults and S3 encryption for logs.
[32:20] Aisha: noted.
[32:40] Martin: any blockers on your side to start the POC?
[32:55] Priya: none, as long as we get the staging access and the benchmark scripts.
[33:15] Daniel: we'll prepare a small runbook for the compatibility validation.
[33:30] Sofia: and a sample terraform module for quickstart.
[33:45] Martin: ok thanks.
[34:00] (wrap-up)
[34:10] Aisha: to recap action items — I'll read them out: 1) Aisha to send SOC2 pack, marketplace checklist, and reference arch by 2026-04-18. 2) Daniel to run benchmark and report by 2026-04-20. 3) Priya to share staging access details and model list by 2026-04-19. 4) Sofia to provide terraform quickstart and network/CIDR guidance by 2026-04-23.
[34:40] Priya: timeline acknowledged.
[34:50] Martin: thanks everyone, this was productive.
[35:00] Luca: thanks.
[35:10] Aisha: we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the benchmark window.
[35:20] (meeting ends, a few seconds of lingering noise)
[44:50] End of recording.
